author: high6
claim: In a nondegenerate triangle ABC, for interior side points D∈BC, E∈CA, F∈AB, normalized barycentric coordinates turn the three cevian incidences into γ/β=BD/DC, α/γ=CE/EA, and β/α=AF/FB. Thus concurrency is equivalent to consistency of these three positive coordinate ratios, which is exactly the condition that their product is 1. [justification_type=calculation; confidence=1.0; is_fragile=false; fragility_reason=""; suggested_followup=none; scope=global]
evidence: For any point X with normalized barycentric coordinates (α,β,γ), the line AD consists exactly of points whose B- and C-coordinates are proportional to those of D; since D=(0,u,v), this is γ/β=v/u=BD/DC whenever β≠0. Cyclically, X∈BE iff α/γ=CE/EA and X∈CF iff β/α=AF/FB. If the cevians concur, their common point cannot lie on a side: for example, a common point on BC would have to equal D from AD∩BC={D}, but BE∩BC={B}, impossible because D is interior; cyclically all coordinates are nonzero. Multiplying the three incidence ratios gives 1. Conversely, if r=BD/DC, s=CE/EA, t=AF/FB satisfy rst=1, the positive barycentric triple (sr,1,r), after normalization, satisfies γ/β=r, α/γ=s, and β/α=1/(sr)=t, so its point lies on AD, BE, and CF.

author: high2
claim: Let p=BD/DC, q=CE/EA, and r=AF/FB. In barycentric coordinates (x,y,z) with respect to the nondegenerate triangle ABC, the three cevian lines AD, BE, CF have equations z=py, x=qz, y=rx, respectively.
evidence: Because D lies in the interior of BC and p=BD/DC>0, D has barycentric coordinates (0,1/(1+p),p/(1+p)); hence the affine line through A=(1,0,0) and D is exactly z=py. Likewise E=(q/(1+q),0,1/(1+q)), so BE is x=qz, and F=(1/(1+r),r/(1+r),0), so CF is y=rx. Affine independence of A,B,C makes barycentric coordinates unique, so these linear equations characterize the lines.

author: high5
claim: In affine barycentric coordinates relative to triangle ABC, if alpha=BD/DC, beta=CE/EA, and gamma=AF/FB, then AD, BE, CF are concurrent if and only if alpha beta gamma=1.
evidence: Because D,E,F are interior points, alpha,beta,gamma are positive. The section formula gives D=(0,1/(1+alpha),alpha/(1+alpha)), E=(beta/(1+beta),0,1/(1+beta)), and F=(1/(1+gamma),gamma/(1+gamma),0). A point (x,y,z), x+y+z=1, lies on AD iff z=alpha y: one direction follows by affine combinations of A and D; conversely xA+yB+zC=xA+(1+alpha)yD when z=alpha y. Analogously BE is x=beta z and CF is y=gamma x. The first two equations and x+y+z=1 have the unique solution P=(alpha beta,1,alpha)/(alpha beta+1+alpha). Hence the three lines have a common point iff P satisfies y=gamma x, equivalently 1=alpha beta gamma.

links.statement: The affine line equations reduce concurrency to one scalar compatibility condition.

author: high3
claim: For unique t,s,u in (0,1) defined by D=(1-t)B+tC, E=sA+(1-s)C, and F=(1-u)A+uB, the required side ratios are BD/DC=t/(1-t), CE/EA=s/(1-s), and AF/FB=u/(1-u).
evidence: Because D divides the segment from B to C at affine parameter t, its distances from B and C are t|BC| and (1-t)|BC|. The same segment-parameter calculation on C-to-A and A-to-B gives the other two formulas. All denominators are positive since D,E,F are interior points, hence t,s,u lie strictly between 0 and 1.

links.statement: Affine side parametrization converts the geometric condition to a scalar identity.

author: high7
claim: For r=BD/DC, s=CE/EA, and t=AF/FB, the three cevian incidences are equivalent at a nonvertex point P with barycentric coordinates (alpha,beta,gamma) to gamma=r beta, alpha=s gamma, and beta=t alpha; moreover, if rst=1 then P=(rs A+B+r C)/(rs+1+r) satisfies all three incidences.
evidence: Since D=(B+rC)/(1+r), membership P in line AD forces the B- and C-barycentric coordinates to occur in ratio 1:r, hence gamma=r beta. Since E=(sA+C)/(1+s), P in line BE gives alpha=s gamma. Since F=(A+tB)/(1+t), P in line CF gives beta=t alpha. For a common point the coordinates are nonzero: for example beta=0 in the first relation would make P=A, but A is not on BE because E is an interior point of CA and B is not on CA; cyclically the other coordinates are nonzero. Thus rst=(gamma/beta)(alpha/gamma)(beta/alpha)=1. Conversely, assume rst=1 and put S=rs+1+r and P=(rs A+B+r C)/S. Then P=(rs/S)A+((1+r)/S)D lies on AD; P=(1/S)B+(r(1+s)/S)E lies on BE; and, since rst=1, P=(r/S)C+(rs(1+t)/S)F lies on CF.

author: high4
claim: In normalized affine barycentric coordinates relative to the nondegenerate triangle ABC, the three cevian lines have equations AD: z=(BD/DC)y, BE: x=(CE/EA)z, and CF: y=(AF/FB)x. Hence they have a common point if and only if (BD/DC)(CE/EA)(AF/FB)=1.
evidence: Because D is interior to BC, D has barycentric coordinates (0,DC/BC,BD/BC), so the line through A=(1,0,0) and D is z=(BD/DC)y. Likewise E=(CE/CA,0,EA/CA) gives BE: x=(CE/EA)z, and F=(FB/AB,AF/AB,0) gives CF: y=(AF/FB)x. If P=(x,y,z) is on all three lines, positivity of the six subsegment lengths and the three line equations show that x,y,z are all nonzero; multiplying z/y=BD/DC, x/z=CE/EA, and y/x=AF/FB gives product 1. Conversely, put d=BD/DC, e=CE/EA, f=AF/FB. If def=1, the positive triple (ed,1,d), normalized by division by ed+1+d, satisfies z=dy, x=ez, and y=fx, so its point lies on all three cevians.
